styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: South Beach sand, Ocean Drive and warm water swims.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Cuban counters, stone crab and Little Havana cafés.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Wynwood murals, Pérez Art Museum and Design District galleries.

stays.why: Walk to the beach, Ocean Drive and Lincoln Road. Best for first-timers who want sand and nightlife on foot.
Free Metromover, good restaurants and bars, and quick links to the airport. Cheaper than the beach.
Leafy, relaxed streets with cafés and marinas. Quieter base, a short drive from the beach.
Pretty Mediterranean-style streets, good dining and the Biltmore. Calm and walkable in the centre.

food: Try Cuban food: a cubano sandwich, ropa vieja and strong cafecito. Little Havana on SW 8th Street (Calle Ocho) is the classic stop.
Stone crab claws are a Miami specialty, in season roughly October to May. Prices are high; check the day's market price.
Eat at a ventanita (walk-up window) for cheap coffee and snacks, often under $10.
Seafood and Latin dishes along the Miami River and in Brickell; book ahead on weekends.
Food halls and markets are good for groups with mixed tastes. Check opening hours on the day.
more_time: Swap a beach afternoon for the Everglades: an airboat tour from the Tamiami Trail side, about an hour's drive each way.
Art lovers can add a day in Wynwood and the Design District for murals and galleries.
Take a day trip to the Florida Keys or Key Biscayne beaches if you want quieter sand.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the beach, Wynwood and Little Havana; add a night for the Everglades or the Keys.

month_notes: Jan: mild and dry, highs near 24°C. Good for walking and the beach on sunny days.
Feb: similar to Jan, around 25°C. Comfortable, with about 11 rain days.
Mar: warming to 26°C. Pleasant spring weather for sightseeing.
Apr: warm at 28°C. Beach days get better; rain days rise slightly.
May: hot and humid, 29°C, with more rain (about 16 days). Plan indoor breaks.
Jun: hot and wet, 30°C and about 22 rain days. Afternoon storms are common.
Jul: hottest stretch, 31°C highs and muggy. Carry water and seek shade.
Aug: hot and the wettest month, about 25 rain days. Watch for storms.
Sep: still hot and wet, 30°C, about 24 rain days. Hurricane season is active; check forecasts.
Oct: easing to 29°C, rain days drop to about 19. Still warm and humid.
Nov: nicer at 27°C with about 13 rain days. Good all-round month.
Dec: mild at 25°C and drier. Busy holiday season; book hotels early.

climate_guide.summary: Subtropical Miami: warm most of the year, with a wet, humid summer and a drier, milder winter.

items.title: Best time: November to April
items.text: Highs around 24–28°C with fewer rain days. Ideal for the beach, walking and outdoor sights.

items.title: Wet season: June to September
items.text: About 22–25 rain days a month. Expect short, heavy afternoon storms; mornings are often clearer.

items.title: Hot and humid summer
items.text: Highs near 30–31°C and lows around 25–26°C. Muggy nights; plan indoor breaks midday.

items.title: Hurricane season
items.text: Runs roughly June to November, peaking late summer and autumn. Check forecasts and travel insurance.

items.title: Beach days
items.text: Comfortable from spring to autumn, but summer sun is strong. Use shade and sunscreen.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, a rain jacket or umbrella for summer, sunscreen and a hat; a light layer for cooler winter evenings.

transit.best: Walk in dense areas; use Uber or Lyft for longer trips and the beach.

modes.text: Metrorail runs elevated trains to downtown, the airport and Dadeland; fare about $2.25. Metromover is free and links downtown and Brickell.
Metrobus covers the county; route S runs downtown to Miami Beach.
Taxis are metered and pricey; Uber and Lyft work well.
Driving is common but traffic and parking are hard; walking is best in dense areas.
Best in dense areas like South Beach, Brickell and Coconut Grove.
Tri-Rail commuter trains link Miami, Fort Lauderdale and West Palm Beach.
